newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Egis plunges on bearish Budapest bourse.
newsitem.headline: Egis plunges on bearish Budapest bourse.

text.p: Hungarian share prices closed lower in bearish sentiment on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Tuesday as profit-taking continued.
The BUX index finished at 3,523.21 points, down 38.47.
"Prices fell because investors took profits," said Robert Stalmayer of AB-Moneta Kft. "Corporate results are not particularly good or bad, so this is an ideal time to lock in profits."
On Tuesday three leading bourse companies released their January-September results, triggering mixed reactions.
Pharmaceuticals Egis disappointed many investors and this was reflected by its plunge to 8,500 forints at the close, down 500.
"The fact that its results were weaker than expected had a key influence in pushing its price lower," Stalmayer said.
The trader expected some more price falls by Egis, although he saw a floor because over half of the company's shares are held by France's Servier SA and therefore the free float is limited.
Chemicals company BorsodChem closed at 3,310 forints, down 35. The market's other chemical company, TVK, advanced five forints to finish at 1,335.
Oil and gas company MOL and meat food processor Pick bucked the trend and closed higher.
MOL was said benefiting from the expected energy price increase and its recent huge deal with Panrusgaz. The share closed at 1,600 forints, up 65.
Pick rose 100 forints to finish at 7,200 after releasing better-than-expected nine-month results on Monday.
